Evaluating Modelling Techniques to Detect Precursors to Landslides from InSAR-Based Data

2026 Honours Project -

# Load packages

library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(MASS)
library(factoextra)
library(gridExtra)
library(cluster)
library(clusterSim)
library(dbscan)
library(dtwclust)
library(patchwork)
library(ggplotify)
library(zoo)


set.seed(1234)

Stage 2: Experimenting with New Processing

We will test a range of transformations on the data before clustering to see if it is able to create a more informative representation of deformation. The approaches are:

  1. Moving average
  2. Piecewise linear regression / linear spline regression
  3. Feature selection
  4. PCA ? - only if time

We will also look at filtering the data based on coherence, as done in Rana et al.’s paper. Adding to our stage 1 clustering baseline, we will apply the same clustering, but on the standardised data. Although, our initial hypothesis with using the standardised data is that it may not be as informative as using the raw displacement values. This is due to all acquisitions being in the same scale, and therefore standardising the data may remove the meaningfulness of measurement difference.

# Helper function for removing baseline date column

  x[, col_sd > 0, drop = FALSE]

2. Moving Averages

We will test three values of window size using moving average:

  • 2: 2 acquisitions are averaged out, meaning one window summarises 12 * 2 = 24 days.

  • 3: 3 acquisitions are averaged out, meaning one window summarises 12 * 3 = 36 days.

  • 5: 5 acquisitions are averaged out, meaning one window summarises 12 * 5 = 60 days.

# Cadia

# MA(2)
cadia_MA2 <- t(apply(cadia_D, 1, function(x) {
  rollmean(x, k = 2, align = "right", fill = NA)
}))

#cadia_MA2 <- cadia_MA2[, -1]

# MA(3)
cadia_MA3 <- t(apply(cadia_D, 1, function(x) {
  rollmean(x, k = 3, align = "right", fill = NA)

Silhouette Score

# Average Silhouette Score Helper Function
avg_sil_score <- function(hc, d_mat, k_vals = 2:5){
  
  avg_sil <- numeric(length(k_vals))
  
  for(i in seq_along(k_vals)){
    
    clusters <- cutree(hc, k = k_vals[i])
    sil_score <- silhouette(clusters, d_mat)
    avg_sil[i] <- mean(sil_score[, 3])
    
  }
  
  data.frame(
    k = k_vals,
    avg_silhouette_score = avg_sil
  )
}

We’ll compute the silhouette score for k = 2, 3, 4 and 5.

# Cadia
cadia_hc_sil <- avg_sil_score(cadia_hc, cadia_dist)

# MA(2)

The moving average dataset of the hierarchical clustering using a window size of 3 achieved the highest average silhouette score for k = 2. Both moving average datasets result in the highest silhouette score at k = 2 and as k increases, the silhouette score decreases.

set.seed(1234)

# Raw
cadia_km_2 <- kmeans(cadia_D, centers = 2, nstart = 20)
cadia_km_3 <- kmeans(cadia_D, centers = 3, nstart = 20)
cadia_km_4 <- kmeans(cadia_D, centers = 4, nstart = 20)

# MA(2)
cadia_MA2_km_2 <- kmeans(cadia_MA2, centers = 2, nstart = 20)
cadia_MA2_km_3 <- kmeans(cadia_MA2, centers = 3, nstart = 20)

cadia_MA2_km_5 <- kmeans(cadia_MA2, centers = 5, nstart = 20)

# MA(3)
cadia_MA3_km_2 <- kmeans(cadia_MA3, centers = 2, nstart = 20)

cadia_MA3_km_4 <- kmeans(cadia_MA3, centers = 4, nstart = 20)
cadia_MA3_km_5 <- kmeans(cadia_MA3, centers = 5, nstart = 20)

set.seed(1234)

# Raw
peru_U_km_2 <- kmeans(peru_D_U, centers = 2, nstart = 20)
peru_U_km_3 <- kmeans(peru_D_U, centers = 3, nstart = 20)

peru_U_km_5 <- kmeans(peru_D_U, centers = 5, nstart = 20)

# MA(2)
peru_U_MA2_km_2 <- kmeans(peru_U_MA2, centers = 2, nstart = 20)

peru_U_MA2_km_4 <- kmeans(peru_U_MA2, centers = 4, nstart = 20)
peru_U_MA2_km_5 <- kmeans(peru_U_MA2, centers = 5, nstart = 20)

# MA(3)
peru_U_MA3_km_2 <- kmeans(peru_U_MA3, centers = 2, nstart = 20)
peru_U_MA3_km_3 <- kmeans(peru_U_MA3, centers = 3, nstart = 20)
peru_U_MA3_km_4 <- kmeans(peru_U_MA3, centers = 4, nstart = 20)
peru_U_MA3_km_5 <- kmeans(peru_U_MA3, centers = 5, nstart = 20)

set.seed(1234)

# Raw
feijao_155_km_2 <- kmeans(feijao_D_155, centers = 2, nstart = 20)
feijao_155_km_3 <- kmeans(feijao_D_155, centers = 3, nstart = 20)
feijao_155_km_4 <- kmeans(feijao_D_155, centers = 4, nstart = 20)
feijao_155_km_5 <- kmeans(feijao_D_155, centers = 5, nstart = 20)

# MA(2)
feijao_155_MA2_km_2 <- kmeans(feijao_155_MA2, centers = 2, nstart = 20)
feijao_155_MA2_km_3 <- kmeans(feijao_155_MA2, centers = 3, nstart = 20)
feijao_155_MA2_km_4 <- kmeans(feijao_155_MA2, centers = 4, nstart = 20)
feijao_155_MA2_km_5 <- kmeans(feijao_155_MA2, centers = 5, nstart = 20)

# MA(3)
feijao_155_MA3_km_2 <- kmeans(feijao_155_MA3, centers = 2, nstart = 20)
feijao_155_MA3_km_3 <- kmeans(feijao_155_MA3, centers = 3, nstart = 20)
feijao_155_MA3_km_4 <- kmeans(feijao_155_MA3, centers = 4, nstart = 20)
feijao_155_MA3_km_5 <- kmeans(feijao_155_MA3, centers = 5, nstart = 20)
```

```r
# Helper function for K-means
avg_sil_score_km <- function(km_models, d_mat){
  
  avg_sil <- numeric(length(km_models))
  
  for(i in seq_along(km_models)){
    
    sil_score <- silhouette(
      km_models[[i]]$cluster,
      d_mat
    )
    
    avg_sil[i] <- mean(sil_score[,3])
    
  }
  
  data.frame(
    k = 2:5,
    avg_silhouette_score = avg_sil
  )
  
}
```

```r
# Davies-Bouldin Index Helper function
dbi_km <- function(data, km_models, k_vals = 2:5) {
  
  db_vals <- numeric(length(km_models))
  
  for (i in seq_along(k_vals)) {
    db_vals[i] <- index.DB(
      data,
      km_models[[i]]$cluster
    )$DB
  }
  
  data.frame(
    k = k_vals,
    davies_bouldin = db_vals
  )
}
```

  cadia_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = \Davies–Bouldin Index: Cadia (Raw)\,
    x = \Number of clusters\,
    y = \Davies–Bouldin index\
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_db_cadia <- ggplot(
  cadia_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = \Davies–Bouldin Index: Cadia (Raw)\,
    x = \Number of clusters\,
    y = \Davies–Bouldin index\
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_db_cadia_MA2 <- ggplot(
  cadia_MA2_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = \Davies–Bouldin Index: Cadia (MA2)\,
    x = \Number of clusters\,
    y = \Davies–Bouldin index\
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

  labs(

    y = \Davies–Bouldin index\
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```r
# Peru (F) -------
p_db_peru_F <- ggplot(
  peru_F_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = "Davies–Bouldin Index: Peru - Failed (Raw)",
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Davies–Bouldin index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_db_peru_F_MA2 <- ggplot(
  peru_F_MA2_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = "Davies–Bouldin Index: Peru - Failed (MA2)",
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Davies–Bouldin index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_db_peru_F_MA3 <- ggplot(
  peru_F_MA3_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = "Davies–Bouldin Index: Peru - Failed (MA3)",
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Davies–Bouldin index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```r
# Peru (U) -------
p_db_peru_U <- ggplot(
  peru_U_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = "Davies–Bouldin Index: Peru - Unfailed (Raw)",
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Davies–Bouldin index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_db_peru_U_MA2 <- ggplot(
  peru_U_MA2_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = "Davies–Bouldin Index: Peru - Unfailed (MA2)",
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Davies–Bouldin index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_db_peru_U_MA3 <- ggplot(
  peru_U_MA3_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = "Davies–Bouldin Index: Peru - Unfailed (MA3)",
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Davies–Bouldin index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```r
# Feijao (T53) -------
p_db_feijao_53 <- ggplot(
  feijao_53_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = "Davies–Bouldin Index: Feijao - T53 (Raw)",
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Davies–Bouldin index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_db_feijao_53_MA2 <- ggplot(
  feijao_53_MA2_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = "Davies–Bouldin Index: Feijao - T53 (MA2)",
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Davies–Bouldin index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_db_feijao_53_MA3 <- ggplot(
  feijao_53_MA3_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = "Davies–Bouldin Index: Feijao - T53 (MA3)",
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Davies–Bouldin index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```r
# Feijao (T155) -------
p_db_feijao_155 <- ggplot(
  feijao_155_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = "Davies–Bouldin Index: Feijao - T155 (Raw)",
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Davies–Bouldin index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_db_feijao_155_MA2 <- ggplot(
  feijao_155_MA2_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = "Davies–Bouldin Index: Feijao - T155 (MA2)",
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Davies–Bouldin index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_db_feijao_155_MA3 <- ggplot(
  feijao_155_MA3_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = "Davies–Bouldin Index: Feijao - T155 (MA3)",
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Davies–Bouldin index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 3. Piecewise Linear Regression

As clustering can be strongly influenced by displacement magnitude and fluctuations, we continue to test methods that smooth out and work with outliers.

The spline approach represents each time series by its rate of deformation over successive time intervals. It may be able to identify and distinguish different deformation behaviours based on changes in velocity/slope.

We'll use the data represented in matrices that still include the baseline date with 0 to use for the first slope.

<!-- rnb-text-begin -->


Piecewise linear models partition the data into segments and fit separate linear regression models to each segment. It allows for broad average trends in the data to be captured while maintaining simplicity and interpretability.

Each segment is divided to make almost linear sections. An index feature is used to model the marginal change of one unit of time. When a series has break points in the trend, we add a knot to each break point:

- A knot feature allows us to inform the model of a change in the trend slope.

- Left to the knot point equals 0, right to the knot is an arbitrage numbers that increase as a function of time.

Instead of treating the columns as observations 1, 2, 3..., we will use elapsed days: 0, 12, 24, 36, 60, etc.


<!-- rnb-text-end -->


<!-- rnb-chunk-begin -->

# Apply spline regression

y <- cadia_D_mat[1, ]

X <- data.frame(time = cadia_time)

for(k in cadia_knots) {
  X[[paste0(\knot_\, k)]] <- pmax(0, cadia_time - k)
}

cadia_model_data <- cbind(data.frame(displacement = y), X)

cadia_test_fit <- lm(displacement ~ ., data = cadia_model_data)
```

# ^^^^ Process as a function

extract_piecewise_slopes <- function(displacement, time, knots) {
  
  # Design matrix
  X <- data.frame(time = time)
  
  for(k in knots) {
    X[[paste0(\knot_\, k)]] <- pmax(0, time - k)
  }
  
  # Add displacement
  model_data <- cbind(
    data.frame(displacement = displacement),
    X
  )
  
  # Fit continuous piecewise-linear regression
  fit <- lm(
    displacement ~ .,
    data = model_data
  )
  
  # Remove intercept
  slope_changes <- coef(fit)[-1]
  
  # Actual slope in each interval
  interval_slopes <- cumsum(slope_changes)
  
  names(interval_slopes) <- paste0(
    \Slope_\, seq_along(interval_slopes)
  )
  
  return(interval_slopes)
}

# ^^^^ Process as a function

extract_piecewise_slopes <- function(displacement, time, knots) {
  
  # Design matrix
  X <- data.frame(time = time)
  
  for(k in knots) {
    X[[paste0(\knot_\, k)]] <- pmax(0, time - k)
  }
  
  # Add displacement
  model_data <- cbind(
    data.frame(displacement = displacement),
    X
  )
  
  # Fit continuous piecewise-linear regression
  fit <- lm(
    displacement ~ .,
    data = model_data
  )
  
  # Remove intercept
  slope_changes <- coef(fit)[-1]
  
  # Actual slope in each interval
  interval_slopes <- cumsum(slope_changes)
  
  names(interval_slopes) <- paste0(
    \Slope_\, seq_along(interval_slopes)
  )
  
  return(interval_slopes)
}

<!-- rnb-output-begin eyJkYXRhIjoiXG48IS0tIHJuYi1zb3VyY2UtYmVnaW4gZXlKa1lYUmhJam9pWUdCZ2NseHVJeUJUZEdGdVpHRnlaQ0JrWlhacFlYUnBiMjRnYjJZZ1pXRmphQ0IwYVcxbElITmxjbWxsYzF4dVkyRmthV0ZmY205M1gzTmtJRHd0SUdGd2NHeDVLR05oWkdsaFgwUXNJREVzSUhOa0tWeHVYRzRqSUZKdmQzTWdkR2hoZENCallXNGdZV04wZFdGc2JIa2dZbVVnYzNSaGJtUmhjbVJwYzJWa1hHNWpZV1JwWVY5MllXeHBaRjl5YjNkeklEd3RJR05oWkdsaFgzSnZkMTl6WkNBaFBTQXdYRzVjYm5OMWJTZ2hZMkZrYVdGZmRtRnNhV1JmY205M2N5bGNibUJnWUNKOSAtLT5cblxuYGBgclxuIyBTdGFuZGFyZCBkZXZpYXRpb24gb2YgZWFjaCB0aW1lIHNlcmllc1xuY2FkaWFfcm93X3NkIDwtIGFwcGx5KGNhZGlhX0QsIDEsIHNkKVxuXG4jIFJvd3MgdGhhdCBjYW4gYWN0dWFsbHkgYmUgc3RhbmRhcmRpc2VkXG5jYWRpYV92YWxpZF9yb3dzIDwtIGNhZGlhX3Jvd19zZCAhPSAwXG5cbnN1bSghY2FkaWFfdmFsaWRfcm93cylcbmBgYFxuXG48IS0tIHJuYi1zb3VyY2UtZW5kIC0tPlxuIn0= -->


<!-- rnb-source-begin eyJkYXRhIjoiYGBgclxuIyBTdGFuZGFyZCBkZXZpYXRpb24gb2YgZWFjaCB0aW1lIHNlcmllc1xuY2FkaWFfcm93X3NkIDwtIGFwcGx5KGNhZGlhX0QsIDEsIHNkKVxuXG4jIFJvd3MgdGhhdCBjYW4gYWN0dWFsbHkgYmUgc3RhbmRhcmRpc2VkXG5jYWRpYV92YWxpZF9yb3dzIDwtIGNhZGlhX3Jvd19zZCAhPSAwXG5cbnN1bSghY2FkaWFfdmFsaWRfcm93cylcbmBgYCJ9 -->

```r
# Standard deviation of each time series
cadia_row_sd <- apply(cadia_D, 1, sd)

# Rows that can actually be standardised
cadia_valid_rows <- cadia_row_sd != 0

sum(!cadia_valid_rows)
```

<!-- rnb-chunk-end -->

```r

  scale(

```r
# dist matrix
cadia_std_dist <- dist(
  cadia_std,
  method = "euclidean"
)

# Ward HC
cadia_std_hc <- hclust(
  cadia_std_dist,
  method = "ward.D2"
)

png(
  "cadia_std_dendrogram.png",
  width = 2400,
  height = 1800,
  res = 300
)

# Dendrogram
plot(
  cadia_std_hc,
  labels = FALSE,
  main = "Cadia: Standardised Raw Data",
  xlab = "",
  sub = "",
  ylab = "Height"
)

dev.off()
```

5.2 K-means Clustering

Elbow Plot

p_cadia_elbow_std <- fviz_nbclust(
  cadia_std,
  kmeans,
  method = "wss"
) +
  ggtitle("Cadia: Standardised")
ggsave(
  "cadia_elbow_std.png",
  p_cadia_elbow_std,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)

Silhouette Score Plot

fviz_nbclust(
  cadia_std,
  kmeans,
  method = "silhouette"
) + 
  ggtitle("Optimal number of clusters: Cadia (Standardised)")
p_cadia_sil_std <- fviz_nbclust(
  cadia_std,
  kmeans,
  method = "silhouette"
) + 
  ggtitle("Optimal number of clusters: Cadia (Standardised)")
ggsave("cadia_sil_std.png",
       p_cadia_sil_std, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)

Applying K-means clustering

set.seed(1234)

cadia_std_km_2 <- kmeans(
  cadia_std,
  centers = 2,
  nstart = 20
)

cadia_std_km_3 <- kmeans(
  cadia_std,
  centers = 3,
  nstart = 20
)

cadia_std_km_4 <- kmeans(
  cadia_std,
  centers = 4,
  nstart = 20
)

cadia_std_km_5 <- kmeans(
  cadia_std,
  centers = 5,
  nstart = 20
)

Silhouette Score

cadia_std_km_sil <- avg_sil_score_km(
  list(cadia_std_km_2,
       cadia_std_km_3,
       cadia_std_km_4,
       cadia_std_km_5),
  cadia_std_dist
)

cadia_std_km_sil

Davies-Bouldin Index

cadia_std_km_db <- dbi_km(
  cadia_std,
  list(cadia_std_km_2,
       cadia_std_km_3,
       cadia_std_km_4,
       cadia_std_km_5)
)

cadia_std_km_db
p_db_cadia_std <- ggplot(
  cadia_std_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = "Davies–Bouldin Index: Cadia (Standardised)",
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Davies–Bouldin index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
ggsave(
  "cadia_dbi_std.png",
  p_db_cadia_std,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)

Apply cluster IDs and export

We have to keep in mind that after standardising, one of the rows was deleted as it led to only zero values. So applying the cluster IDs is a different process here.

# Create empty cols
cadia$std_km_2 <- NA_integer_
cadia$std_km_3 <- NA_integer_
cadia$std_km_4 <- NA_integer_
cadia$std_km_5 <- NA_integer_

# Fill only rows that were included in standardisation
cadia$std_km_2[cadia_valid_rows] <- cadia_std_km_2$cluster
cadia$std_km_3[cadia_valid_rows] <- cadia_std_km_3$cluster
cadia$std_km_4[cadia_valid_rows] <- cadia_std_km_4$cluster
cadia$std_km_5[cadia_valid_rows] <- cadia_std_km_5$cluster
cadia[7424, c(
  "std_km_2",
  "std_km_3",
  "std_km_4",
  "std_km_5"
)]
table(cadia$std_km_2, useNA = "ifany")
write.csv(
  cadia,
  "cadia_std_km.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
